subject: BYO Key dual-wallet escrow provisioning & network zoning questions

Subject: Dual-wallet BYO escrow provisioning questions

Hi David,

Thanks again for agreeing to review our dual-wallet escrow approach for BYO keys in your Private deployment offering. We ran the design by the engineering team and have a couple of implementation constraints we need to confirm before the PoC: 

1) Network flow: we expect the HSM appliance (customer-controlled) to initiate outbound mTLS connections to Saltstone's escrow ingestion endpoint for split-key escrow. Can you confirm your preferred egress model for on-prem and VPC installs (NAT outbound, egress proxy, or customer-managed breakout)? Also can you support static outbound IPs / allowlisting?

2) Import APIs: our escrow service supports PKCS#11 wrapping and an HSM-vendor push model (HSM opens TLS session, Saltstone performs remote wrap). Which integration points do you support today in your Private bundle?

3) Operator separation & rotation: for our threat model we require automated rotation windows with a one-hour maintenance slot and operator actions to be recorded in an audit log with signed attestations. Can you confirm audit log retention and whether Redwood can emit signed audit events for key import/rotation?

4) Attestation & transport: we prefer transport via mTLS + signed timestamps. Will your on-prem package allow outbound mTLS to our endpoint and present a client cert from the HSM? Are there extra proxy/auth steps required?

Attached are a short checklist and our escrow term sheet for reference.

Attachments: saltstone-byo-specs.pdf (application/pdf), saltstone-byo-escrow-term-sheet.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

If it helps we can run a short, focused runbook review call (30m) next week.

Priya —

Appreciate the detail and the checklist. Quick answers inline below, plus a proposed agenda for the runbook review call. 

On Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 09:12 AM Saltstone Systems <security@saltstone.com> wrote:
> 1) Network flow: we expect the HSM appliance (customer-controlled) to initiate outbound mTLS connections to Saltstone's escrow ingestion endpoint for split-key escrow. Can you confirm your preferred egress model for on-prem and VPC installs (NAT outbound, egress proxy, or customer-managed breakout)?

For Redwood Private we typically support two patterns depending on customer preference:
- VPC (cloud-hosted private): HSMs live in a customer-managed private subnet. Outbound egress goes through a managed egress proxy or NAT gateway; customers can request static outbound egress IPs via cross-account NAT or a managed egress appliance.
- On-prem: HSMs run behind the customer's perimeter; our package assumes outbound-only connections from the HSM to an allowlisted Saltstone endpoint. We can support mTLS via customer-supplied client certs and recommend an egress proxy in high-security environments.

> 2) Import APIs: our escrow service supports PKCS#11 wrapping and an HSM-vendor push model (HSM opens TLS session, Saltstone performs remote wrap). Which integration points do you support today in your Private bundle?

We support both flows for common HSM vendors (Thales/Cavium, Utimaco). For PKCS#11 wrap/unwrapped key import we have a small operator-side tool that can be run from the admin bastion to orchestrate the wrapping handshake. For vendor push models we can permit direct HSM-initiated sessions to the escrow endpoint (subject to network allowlist and mTLS).

> 3) Operator separation & rotation: for our threat model we require automated rotation windows with a one-hour maintenance slot and operator actions to be recorded in an audit log with signed attestations. Can you confirm audit log retention and whether Redwood can emit signed audit events for key import/rotation?

We emit structured audit events to the customer audit log with configurable retention (default 90 days; enterprise option up to 7 years). We can sign key-import/rotation events with an HSM-stored signing key and provide an attestation bundle that includes the event hash, timestamp (RFC3339), and operator principal. We'll need to map the operator identity to our RBAC model (bastion SSH session or short-lived operator tokens).

> 4) Attestation & transport: we prefer transport via mTLS + signed timestamps. Will your on-prem package allow outbound mTLS to our endpoint and present a client cert from the HSM? Are there extra proxy/auth steps required?

Yes — outbound mTLS from the HSM to Saltstone is supported. If the HSM cannot present the client cert directly, we can proxy the CSR flow through our operator tool running on the bastion (CSR is generated from HSM, signed by operator, and then used for mTLS).

Proposed next steps / call agenda (30m):
- Confirm IP allowlist and egress pattern (10m)
- Walkthrough of PKCS#11 vs vendor-push import (10m)
- Auditing/attestation artifact formats and retention policy (10m)

I'll loop in Monica and Soojin to capture network/security constraints and to schedule the call. Are you available Thu/Fri next week (7/8–7/9)?

David / team —

Thanks for the response, David. Copying a short checklist I want us to confirm before the runbook review with Saltstone: 

- Dedicated HSM subnet: Create a /28 (minimum) private subnet in customer VPC for HSMs and operator bastion; no inbound internet routes.
- Security Groups / FW: Outbound-only 443 to Saltstone IP ranges (to be provided). Inbound SSH only from our central bastion (jitted access).
- Static Egress IPs: customer must provision static NAT IPs or use our managed egress appliance; document IPs in the allowlist.
- Client certificate flow: Prefer direct HSM client cert. If not possible, plan CSR proxy flow via operator bastion.
- Audit artefacts: capture (a) key-id, (b) rotation-type, (c) operator-principal, (d) attestation-sig, (e) timestamp. Store artifacts in customer-controlled S3 with server-side encryption.
- Rotation window: default one-hour maintenance; recommend rolling rotations across replica groups to maintain availability.

I'll open JIRA-SEC-4123 with the items above and attach a network sketch. Also propose we add a short checklist item that the customer's security team performs an outbound egress test to Saltstone's test endpoint before production provisioning.

- David: confirm available slots (Thu/Fri 7/8–7/9) for the runbook review.

- Hannah: draft the attestation event schema for review.
